title: Demonstration 3: Paired Multiomics (scRNA-seq + scATAC-seq) Simulation Evaluation
text: Single-cell multiomics co-assay technologies (10x Chromium Multiome, SHARE-seq, SNARE-seq) enable simultaneous measurement gene expression (scRNA-seq) chromatin accessibility (scATAC-seq) exact individual cells. joint profiling provides unprecedented resolution transcriptional regulation, enhancer-promoter dynamics, epigenomic priming. However, simulating paired single-cell multiomics presents distinct computational statistical challenges beyond unimodal simulation: * Cell-Level Cross-Modality Pairing: Simulated data must preserve 1--1 correspondence cellular barcodes RNA ATAC modalities—column RNA count matrix represents exact physical cell column ATAC matrix. * Biological Coupling & Cross-Modal Concordance: Open chromatin regulatory loci typically precedes correlates gene transcription. Simulation algorithms must preserve biological correlation peak accessibility target gene expression without introducing synthetic alignment artifacts. * Asymmetric Sparsity & Modality Noise Profiles: scRNA-seq expression exhibits continuous distribution count-dependent logistic dropouts (80–90% zeros), whereas scATAC-seq peak accessibility near-binary subject extreme diploid-limited sparsity (90–98% zeros). Simulators must balance divergent biophysical properties concurrently. * Unified Latent Geometry: Joint low-dimensional embeddings must capture continuous developmental kinetics distinct cell-type clusters congruently across modalities. scSimEval provides standardized, reference-based benchmarking framework evaluate paired single-cell multiomics simulations across 8 active evaluation categories comprising 56 curated metrics: Category : Distributional Properties — Univariate statistical distances (Wasserstein, Kolmogorov–Smirnov, MAD, Bhattacharyya) evaluated across cell-level library sizes, gene expression rates, peak accessibility frequencies modalities. Category II: Sparsity & Zero-Inflation Dynamics — Logistic dropout curves scRNA-seq quadratic accessibility-sparsity curves scATAC-seq, quantifying curve RMSE R^2 fit discrepancy. Category III: Cellular Manifold & Clustering Concordance — Latent manifold preservation, Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD), Generative Precision & Recall, Average Silhouette Width (ASW), Adjusted Rand Index (ARI), Normalized Mutual Information (NMI). Category IV: Technical Variation & Batch Mixing Dynamics — Batch Silhouette Width, Principal Component Regression (PCR\ R^2), Cell-Specific Mixing Score (CMS), Inverse Simpson’s Index (ISI). Category V: Biological Signal & Differential Fidelity — Pseudobulk edgeR-QLF statistical testing across biological replicates assessing differentially expressed genes (DEG) differentially accessible peaks (DA). Category VI: Multiomics Integration & Alignment — Cross-modality feature correlation preservation, joint-embedding Batch ASW, joint Cell-Type ASW, within-cell-type k-NN graph connectivity, joint clustering ARI/NMI. Category VII: Trajectory & Lineage Topology — Milestone graph topology similarity (, edge-flip), geodesic distance correlation, branch assignment fidelity. Category VIII: Computational Scalability & Efficiency — Hardware-normalized execution runtime (core_seconds), resident peak memory per allocated core (memory_per_core_mib), simulation throughput (cells/second), speed-memory trade-offs.

title: Demonstration 3: Paired Multiomics (scRNA-seq + scATAC-seq) Simulation Evaluation
text: Raw metrics span disparate physical units (distances, runtimes, MiB RAM, correlation coefficients). scSimEval standardizes raw metrics direction-aware fidelity scores [0, 1], 1.0 indicates ideal biological fidelity: * distance error metrics lower values represent superior accuracy (e.g., Wasserstein, MMD, dropout RMSE), scores inverted: \text{Score} = \exp(-\gamma \cdot \text{distance}). * bounded concordance indices higher values represent superior fidelity (e.g., ARI, NMI, Generative Precision, DA ROC-AUC), scores scaled linearly [0, 1]. * mixing balance metrics values closer zero indicate optimal batch mixing without clustering artifacts (e.g., Batch Silhouette), scores centered symmetrically.

text: Benchmarking 6 simulators empirical Rice Seed paired multiomics co-assay reveals key performance characteristics trade-offs: Top Overall Fidelity (scDesign3): Ranked #1 overall (Average Fidelity: 73.4%), achieving top scores across Distributional Properties (Category ), Sparsity Dynamics (Category II), Differential Fidelity (Category V). probabilistic copula framework accurately captures marginal expression accessibility distributions maintaining realistic dropout rates. Superior Cross-Modal Alignment (scMultiSim): Ranked #1 Multiomics Integration & Alignment (Category VI: 85.1%). explicitly modeling regulatory gene-peak interactions kinetic dynamics, scMultiSim excelled preserving biological coupling chromatin accessibility transcriptional output. Lightweight & High-Throughput Alternative (Matilda & scMoMtF): scMoMtF completed just 7.5 seconds (160 MB RAM) Matilda 31.8 seconds (167 MB RAM), achieving high cellular manifold preservation (Category III) strong integration fidelity (~79.1–79.7%) minimal computational overhead. Parametric vs. Generative Models: generative adversarial frameworks (scCross) simulate non-linear manifolds well, probabilistic copula models (scDesign3) mechanistic kinetic simulators (scMultiSim) remain superior benchmark scenarios requiring exact biological reference concordance ground-truth validation.

title: Demonstration 5: Analyzing Pre-Saved Benchmark Results (.rds)
text: multi-tissue multi-simulator benchmarking studies executed high-performance computing (HPC) clusters, computing full 56-metric evaluation suite across dozens dataset-simulator pairs computationally intensive. evaluations serialized .rds files via saveRDS(), scSimEval enables instant reloading, cross-dataset consolidation, custom leaderboard ranking, publication-grade visualization — without re-computing single metric. demonstration illustrates complete downstream .rds workflow using 3 independently saved Rice paired multiomics benchmark sessions (Flag, Leaf, Root tissues), containing 6 simulators (scDesign3, MOSim, scCross, scMultiSim, Matilda, scMoMtF) evaluated across 8 canonical categories (2,154 metric evaluations per tissue; 6,462 total rows).

title: Demonstration 5: Analyzing Pre-Saved Benchmark Results (.rds)
text: saved session .rds archive contains standardized benchmark_df, dataset summaries, metadata. Using combine_benchmark_results(), multiple .rds files computed separate nodes different times can merged unified cross-tissue benchmark table seconds: Let’s inspect consolidated cross-tissue object structure:
code:
library(scSimEval)  # 1. Load three independently saved benchmark sessions (zero re-computation) flag_sess <- readRDS("rice_Flag_vs_all_6_simulators.rds") leaf_sess <- readRDS("rice_Leaf_vs_all_6_simulators.rds") root_sess <- readRDS("rice_Root_vs_all_6_simulators.rds")  # 2. Extract their tidy benchmark tables raw_dfs <- list(   Flag = flag_sess$benchmark_df,   Leaf = leaf_sess$benchmark_df,   Root = root_sess$benchmark_df )  # 3. Consolidate into a single cross-tissue benchmark with re-normalized scores combined_res <- combine_benchmark_results(   list_of_benchmarks   = raw_dfs,   filter_gold_standard = TRUE,   recompute_normalized = TRUE )  combined_df <- standardize_benchmark_categories(combined_res$granular_benchmark_table) saveRDS(combined_df, "scSimEval_combined_benchmark_results.rds") cat("Total consolidated metric rows:", nrow(combined_df), "

title: Demonstration 2: scATAC-seq Simulation Evaluation
text: Single-cell assay transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq) profiling provides profound insights epigenomic regulation, chromatin architecture, transcription factor occupancy cellular resolution. contrast single-cell transcriptomics, scATAC-seq peak accessibility data present distinct statistical biophysical features: * Extreme Sparsity: 90% 98% values peak--cell matrices zeroes due diploid limit (2 genomic copies per cell) technical capture dropouts. * Near-Binary Open/Closed Dynamics: Raw counts predominantly reflect discrete accessibility (0, 1, 2 transposase insertions) rather continuous high-magnitude expression. * TF-IDF Normalization: Feature transformation relies Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) rather \log_2(\text{CPM} + 1) balance locus-specific accessibility global sequencing depth. * Quadratic Accessibility-Sparsity Relationship: empirical datasets, locus detection frequency adheres characteristic quadratic curve respect mean accessibility. ensure computational pipelines, peak-calling algorithms, cell-type classifiers developed synthetic data biologically reliable, researchers require rigorous tools validate faithfully simulated scATAC-seq data reproduce real biological experiments. scSimEval provides standardized, reference-based benchmarking framework systematically quantify single-cell epigenomic simulation fidelity. unimodal scATAC-seq, scSimEval evaluates synthetic data across 6 active evaluation categories: Category : Distributional Properties — Univariate statistical distances (Wasserstein, Kolmogorov–Smirnov, MAD, Bhattacharyya) evaluated across cell-level insertion sums, peak detection rates, Signac/simPIC-standard TF-IDF transformed accessibility coordinates. Category II: Sparsity & Zero-Inflation Dynamics — Quadratic accessibility-sparsity curve parameters (curve RMSE, R^2 fit discrepancy) zero-probability profile preservation. Category III: Cellular Manifold & Clustering Concordance — Latent epigenomic geometry preservation, Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD), Generative Precision & Recall, Average Silhouette Width (ASW), Adjusted Rand Index (ARI), Normalized Mutual Information (NMI). Category IV: Technical Variation & Batch Mixing Dynamics — Batch Silhouette Width, Principal Component Regression (PCR\ R^2), Cell-Specific Mixing Score (CMS), Inverse Simpson’s Index (ISI), cross-batch cell-type classification transfer F1. Category V: Biological Signal & Differential Accessibility (DA) Fidelity — Pseudobulk edgeR-QLF statistical testing across biological replicates assessing null p-value uniformity, marker peak detection accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC. Category VIII: Computational Scalability & Efficiency — Hardware-normalized execution runtime (core_seconds), resident peak memory per allocated core (memory_per_core_mib), simulation throughput (cells/second), speed-memory trade-offs. Note Categories VI & VII: Category VI (Multiomics Integration & Alignment) evaluates cross-modality latent alignment paired unpaired scRNA-seq scATAC-seq co-assays, Category VII (Trajectory & Lineage Topology) requires continuous transcriptional kinetics. naturally inactive unimodal scATAC-seq evaluations.

title: Demonstration 1: scRNA-seq Simulation Evaluation
text: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) simulation algorithms essential evaluating computational pipelines, developing clustering methods, benchmarking differential expression detectors controlled ground-truth conditions. However, ensure findings translate reliably real biological data, researchers must rigorously evaluate faithfully synthetic datasets replicate empirical experiments. scSimEval provides standardized, reference-based benchmarking framework systematically quantify single-cell simulation accuracy. unimodal scRNA-seq, scSimEval evaluates synthetic data across 7 active evaluation categories comprising 44 curated metrics: Category : Distributional Properties (14 metrics) — Univariate bivariate statistical distances (Wasserstein, Kolmogorov–Smirnov, MAD, Bhattacharyya, nearest-neighbor divergence) across cell-level gene-level properties. Category II: Sparsity & Zero-Inflation Dynamics (4 metrics) — Logistic dropout curve parameters (midpoint error x_0, slope error k, fit discrepancy R^2) excess zero proportions. Category III: Cellular Manifold & Clustering Concordance (8 metrics) — High-dimensional geometry preservation, Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD), Generative Precision & Recall, Average Silhouette Width (ASW), Clustering Deviation Index (CDI), Adjusted Rand Index (ARI), Normalized Mutual Information (NMI). Category IV: Technical Variation & Batch Mixing Dynamics (5 metrics) — Batch Silhouette Width, Principal Component Regression (PCR\ R^2), Cell-Specific Mixing Score (CMS), Inverse Simpson’s Index (ISI), cross-batch cell-type classification F1. Category V: Biological Signal & Differential Expression (DEG) Fidelity (6 metrics) — Pseudobulk edgeR-QLF statistical testing assessing null p-value uniformity, marker gene detection accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC. Category VII: Trajectory & Lineage Topology (5 metrics) — HVG-filtered dynverse lineage modeling measuring milestone graph topology similarity (, edge-flip), geodesic distance correlation, branch assignment F1, Random Forest driver feature importance correlation. Category VIII: Computational Scalability & Efficiency (2 metrics) — Hardware-normalized execution runtime (core_seconds) resident peak memory per allocated core (memory_per_core_mib). Note Category VI: Category VI (Multiomics Integration & Alignment) evaluates cross-modality latent alignment scRNA-seq scATAC-seq co-assays, naturally inactive unimodal scRNA-seq evaluations.

title: Demonstration 4: Unpaired Multiomics (scRNA-seq + scATAC-seq) Simulation Evaluation
text: unpaired single-cell multiomics designs, gene expression (scRNA-seq) chromatin accessibility (scATAC-seq) profiled separate, non-overlapping populations single cells harvested biological tissue sibling aliquots. Unlike paired co-assays, cell barcode RNA count matrix correspond cell barcode ATAC matrix, two modalities frequently differ total cell count, batch structure, annotation granularity. Simulating evaluating unpaired multiomics introduces distinct methodological requirements: * Unequal Cell Counts & Independent Barcodes: Evaluators must compare RNA ATAC layers independently without assuming 1--1 cell correspondence. * Shared-Manifold Alignment Without Cell Pairing: Cross-modality coherence (Category VI) assessed shared biological population integrated latent embedding level (joint cell-type alignment, batch mixing, graph connectivity) rather direct cell--cell feature pairing. * Modality-Specific Scalability Accounting: simulators (scMultiSim, scCross) simulate modalities single unified run, whereas modular frameworks (scDesign3) fit simulate scRNA-seq scATAC-seq separate jobs distinct CPU core allocations memory footprints. scSimEval natively supports combined modality-separated resource tracking. scSimEval handles unpaired designs automatically pairing = "unpaired" evaluate_multiomics_accuracy(), evaluating 8 active categories: 1. Category : Distributional Properties — Independent univariate distributional distances across RNA genes ATAC peaks. 2. Category II: Sparsity & Zero-Inflation Dynamics — Logistic dropout modeling RNA quadratic accessibility-sparsity curve fitting ATAC. 3. Category III: Cellular Manifold & Clustering Concordance — Modality-specific manifold geometry, MMD, Generative Precision & Recall, ASW, ARI, NMI. 4. Category IV: Technical Variation & Batch Mixing Dynamics — Batch Silhouette Width, Principal Component Regression (PCR\ R^2), CMS, ISI per modality. 5. Category V: Biological Signal & Differential Fidelity — Pseudobulk edgeR-QLF differentially expressed genes (DEG) differentially accessible peaks (DA). 6. Category VI: Multiomics Integration & Alignment — Cross-modality latent space alignment, joint Cell-Type ASW, joint Batch ASW, within-cell-type graph connectivity integrated embeddings. 7. Category VII: Trajectory & Lineage Topology — Transcriptomic lineage topology (, edge-flip, geodesic correlation, branch F1). 8. Category VIII: Computational Scalability & Efficiency — Hardware-normalized core_seconds memory_per_core_mib, supporting unified modality-separated (RNA + ATAC) execution logs.

what: 2. Running the Unpaired Multiomics Benchmarking Pipeline
title: Demonstration 4: Unpaired Multiomics (scRNA-seq + scATAC-seq) Simulation Evaluation
text: Setting pairing = "unpaired" evaluate_multiomics_accuracy() activates independent modality evaluation unpaired joint-embedding integration scoring. exact workflow demonstrating combined (scMultiSim, scCross) modality-separated (scDesign3) resource logging:
code: library(scSimEval)  # Validate empirical reference (extracts independent RNA and ATAC SCE layers + colData) ref_val <- validate_multiomics_input(   readRDS("soy_hypocotyl_reference_integrated_combined.rds"),   "Soybean Hypocotyl (Unpaired)" )  # Example A: Combined resource tracking (scMultiSim / scCross) eval_scmultisim <- evaluate_multiomics_accuracy(   ref_multi         = list(RNA = ref_val$m1_obj, ATAC = ref_val$m2_obj),   sim_multi         = list(RNA = sim_val$m1_obj, ATAC = sim_val$m2_obj),   pairing           = "unpaired",   elapsed_time      = 216.804,   time_unit         = "seconds",   memory_mb         = 2774.70,   memory_unit       = "MiB",   sim_cores         = 16L,   compute_bivariate = TRUE,   threads           = 16L,   verbose           = FALSE )  # Example B: Separate modality resource tracking (scDesign3) eval_scdesign3 <- evaluate_multiomics_accuracy(   ref_multi         = list(RNA = ref_val$m1_obj, ATAC = ref_val$m2_obj),   sim_multi         = list(RNA = sim_d3$m1_obj,  ATAC = sim_d3$m2_obj),   pairing           = "unpaired",   separate_resources = list(     rna  = list(elapsed_time = 89.19,  memory_mb = 2190.40, time_unit = "seconds", memory_unit = "MiB", sim_cores = 16L),     atac = list(elapsed_time = 268.28, memory_mb = 9334.00, time_unit = "seconds", memory_unit = "MiB", sim_cores = 4L)   ),   compute_bivariate = TRUE,   threads           = 16L,   verbose           = FALSE )

title: Demonstration 4: Unpaired Multiomics (scRNA-seq + scATAC-seq) Simulation Evaluation
text: Evaluating unpaired Soybean Hypocotyl multiomics highlights distinct strengths across methodological families: Best Overall Balance (scCross, 54.4%): Led overall leaderboard achieving top scores Trajectory & Lineage Topology (0.799), Batch Mixing Dynamics (0.757), Differential Signal Fidelity (0.494), though substantially higher runtime cost (2,005 s across 16 cores). Highest Marginal & Manifold Fidelity (scDesign3, 51.0%): Dominated Distributional Properties (0.923), Sparsity & Zero-Inflation Dynamics (0.857), Cellular Manifold Concordance (0.666), matching empirical RNA sparsity (92.92% vs. 92.91%) ATAC median library size (2,102 vs. 2,096) high precision. fits RNA ATAC separately, ATAC simulation requires higher per-core RAM (9,334 MiB across 4 cores). Best Scalability & Unpaired Integration (scMultiSim, 40.1%): Achieved highest Computational Scalability score (0.973; 216.8 s combined runtime) strongest Unpaired Multiomics Integration & Alignment score (0.600), making well-suited rapid cross-modal integration benchmarking.

what: Overview of the scSimEval Evaluation Suite
title: Comprehensive Catalog of the 56 Evaluation Measures
text: Single-cell multiomics simulation algorithms central computational biology. let researchers benchmark new bioinformatic methods, optimize experimental designs, test analytical workflows without expense wet-lab sequencing. However, simulator truly useful, synthetic data generates must faithfully mirror real biology across multiple dimensions—basic gene expression distributions complex cell-cell interactions, batch variations, developmental trajectories. scSimEval provides rigorous, standardized, reference-based benchmarking framework evaluate simulation quality. Rather relying single overall score handful summary statistics, assesses synthetic datasets across 56 curated evaluation measures organized 8 foundational categories. Every measure calculated directly comparing silico simulated dataset empirical biological reference dataset across single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), single-cell ATAC sequencing (scATAC-seq), joint multiomics (paired unpaired RNA + ATAC) modalities.

title: Getting Started with scSimEval: Benchmarking Single-Cell Simulations in Bioconductor
text: scSimEval provides unified, standardized benchmarking suite evaluate closely synthetic single-cell datasets reproduce empirical biological references across scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, paired/unpaired single-cell multiomics.

title: Getting Started with scSimEval: Benchmarking Single-Cell Simulations in Bioconductor
text: scSimEval built directly Bioconductor core data structures statistical infrastructure: Data representation: Accepts SingleCellExperiment (multi-modal SingleCellExperiment objects altExp()), reading cell-type (cell_type) replicate/batch (batch) annotations directly SummarizedExperiment::colData(). Users starting Seurat objects can convert one line via Seurat::.SingleCellExperiment(). Parallel & sparse execution: Uses BiocParallel Matrix sparse S4 methods scalable memory-efficient evaluation. Downstream statistical engines: Integrates edgeR (pseudobulk quasi-likelihood differential expression/accessibility), CDI (Clustering Deviation Index), scater scuttle (QC normalization utilities), CellMixS (cell-specific batch mixing).

title: Getting Started with scSimEval: Benchmarking Single-Cell Simulations in Bioconductor
text: splatter: Primarily focuses simulating scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., Splat, Lun, Simple models) provides basic property comparisons via compareSCEs(). scSimEval complements splatter serving simulator-agnostic evaluator benchmarks simulator output across 56 metrics 8 categories—spanning distributional distances, dropout/sparsity curves, clustering concordance, batch mixing, pseudobulk differential fidelity, trajectory topology, cross-modal integration, hardware-normalized scalability. countsimQC: Generates visual comparisons distributional summaries synthetic real count matrices (primarily bulk unimodal RNA-seq). scSimEval extends beyond marginal count QC assess single-cell downstream structure (clustering ARI/NMI/CDI, batch PCR/CMS/ISI, pseudobulk DEG/DA ROC-AUC, scATAC-seq TF-IDF accessibility, paired/unpaired RNA+ATAC integration, core_seconds / memory_per_core_mib efficiency).

title: Compute Clustering Deviation Index (CDI) for Single-Cell Clustering Evaluation — calc_cdi
text: Evaluates unsupervised goodness--fit single-cell clustering labels directly count matrices using official Bioconductor CDI package (Fang et al., Genome Biology, 2022; DOI: 10.1186/s13059-022-02825-5). CDI models UMI counts cluster- gene-specific Negative Binomial distributions adjusted cell size factors, returning AIC- BIC-penalized deviation scores.

code: calc_cdi(   counts,   cluster_labels,   batch_label = NULL,   size_factors = NULL,   nfeature = 500L,   method = c("wds", "vst"),   zp_threshold = 0.95,   lrt_pval_threshold = 0.01,   max_cells = 1000L,   normalize_per_obs = TRUE,   threads = 1L,   seed = 42L,   top_features = NULL )

NULL, computed via CDI::size_factor(). nfeature Integer number informative feature genes select via CDI::feature_gene_selection() (default 500L, per Fang et al., 2022). method Feature selection method passed CDI::feature_gene_selection(): "wds" (Working Dispersion Score, default) "vst". zp_threshold Numeric zero-proportion cutoff (0, 1) used pre-filter ultra-sparse features prior WDS selection (default 0.95). title: Calculate Kernel Density Overlap Value (OV) — calc_overlap

what: Evaluate Multiomics Integration & Cross-Modal Alignment Fidelity (Category VI) — evaluate_multiomics_integration
title: Evaluate Multiomics Integration & Cross-Modal Alignment Fidelity (Category VI) — evaluate_multiomics_integration
text: Evaluates multiomics integration cross-modal alignment fidelity simulated single-cell multiomics data across 5 gold-standard integration metrics extracted key single-cell benchmarking suites (scib, scMultiSim, scCross, Matilda, scMoMtF): Batch ASW (batch_asw): Average Silhouette Width evaluating batch mixing within cell types (scib, scMultiSim). Cell-Type ASW (cell_type_asw): Average Silhouette Width evaluating cell-type bio-conservation multiomics space (scCross, scib). Graph Connectivity (graph_connectivity): Relative size largest connected component k-NN graph cell type (scCross, scMultiSim, scib). ARI (ari): Adjusted Rand Index comparing joint multiomics clustering ground-truth cell types (scib, scCross, scMultiSim, Matilda, scMoMtF). NMI (nmi): Normalized Mutual Information quantifying information concordance joint clustering cell types (scib, scCross, scMultiSim, Matilda, scMoMtF).

what: Full Category VII Trajectory & Lineage Topology Evaluation (dynverse Workflow) — evaluate_trajectory_metrics
title: Full Category VII Trajectory & Lineage Topology Evaluation (dynverse Workflow) — evaluate_trajectory_metrics
text: Evaluates trajectory lineage preservation using standardized dynverse benchmarking framework (Saelens et al., Nature Biotechnology, 2019): Standardized cell outlier QC (3 MADs), low-expression gene filtering         (\(\ge 5\%\) cells, mean \(> 0.02\)), HVG selection (empirical mean-variance decomposition). Shared HVG PCA projection Docker-free Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) milestone         trajectory inference continuous cell--milestone geodesic distances. Five complementary trajectory metrics: (Hamming-Ipsen-Mikhailov similarity),         edge_flip (minimum edge flip similarity), geodesic_correlation,         F1_branches, wcor_features (ranger Random Forest feature         importance weighted correlation num_trees = 10000 1 percent mtry).

what: scSimEval: Unified Benchmarking and Accuracy Evaluation for Single-Cell Multiomics Simulation Methods — scSimEval-package
title: scSimEval: Unified Benchmarking and Accuracy Evaluation for Single-Cell Multiomics Simulation Methods — scSimEval-package
text: simple unified evaluation toolkit benchmarking single-cell multiomics data simulation methods. Evaluates realistic simulated data compared real biological datasets across three multiomics experimental designs: () paired multiomics (simultaneous co-assay identical cells, e.g. 10x Chromium Multiome, SHARE-seq, SNARE-seq), unlocks full Category 6 multiomics integration cross-modal alignment suite (joint-embedding Batch ASW, Cell-Type ASW, Graph Connectivity, Integration ARI, Integration NMI); (ii) unpaired multiomics (independent scRNA-seq scATAC-seq profiled separate cells tissue), supported per-modality unimodal evaluation (Categories 1-5, 7, 8) joint-embedding integration fidelity; (iii) mosaic multiomics (partial co-measurement subset cells modalities, e.g. DOGMA-seq mosaic pooling designs), handled evaluating paired unimodal cell fractions across 8 canonical categories. toolkit quantifies simulation realism using 56 evaluation measures organized 8 canonical categories: (1) Distributional Properties: 10 univariate metrics (Wasserstein, KS, MAD, MAE, RMSE, Bhattacharyya, KDE-ISE, Runs statistic, NN mismatch, Inter-dataset silhouette) 4 bivariate metrics (Fasano-Franceschini 2D KS, 2D EMD, 2D NN mismatch, 2D Inter-dataset silhouette) evaluated across 7 cell-level, 7 feature-level, 4 bivariate property pairs, (2) Sparsity & Zero-Inflation Dynamics: logistic dropout curve midpoint/slope/R2 (scRNA-seq), quadratic accessibility-sparsity curve RMSE/R2 (scATAC-seq), posterior excess zero weight discrepancy, (3) Cellular Manifold & Clustering Concordance: MMD, Generative Precision/Recall, Silhouette ASW, Clustering Deviation Index (CDI), Neighborhood Purity, ARI, NMI (auxiliary Davies-Bouldin Index), (4) Technical Variation & Batch Mixing Dynamics: Batch Silhouette, PCR R2, CMS, Inverse Simpson Index (ISI), Cross-Batch F1, (5) Biological Signal & Differential Fidelity: pseudobulk edgeR-QLF null P-value uniformity, accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC across parallel scRNA-seq DE scATAC-seq DA sub-categories, (6) Multiomics Integration & Alignment: joint-embedding Batch ASW, Cell-Type ASW, Graph Connectivity, Integration ARI, Integration NMI, (7) Trajectory & Lineage Topology: HVG-filtered dynverse benchmark (Saelens et al., 2019) comprising topology similarity, edge flip similarity, geodesic distance correlation, branch assignment F1, Random Forest feature importance weighted correlation (wcor_features), (8) Computational Scalability & Efficiency: core-normalized execution runtime (core_seconds) memory footprint per allocated core (memory_per_core_mib), automated multi-core scaling unified memory_mb resource benchmarking. Includes non-linear low-dimensional cell embedding projections (UMAP, t-SNE, PCA) quantitative cluster separability (Silhouette) fidelity (ARI) metrics, automated score normalization, leaderboards, publication visualizations. Interactive GUI exploration available via companion scSimEvalStudio package.
